content.text: The local grammar and state-machine checks pass, including malformed-request fuzzing. Next I’m measuring worst-case replay workloads and reviewing strict-envelope behavior under the actual isolated invocation.

arguments.command:
cat > /app/bench_local.py <<'PY'
import json,subprocess,time,sys,resource
sys.path.insert(0,'/app')
from test_local import req,base
# 10k valid requests, distinct keys, around 8 MB aggregate, 150 ignored header rows each
extra=[('X','a') for _ in range(145)]
w=req(extra=extra,body=b'')
# correct CL auto zero
ws=[]
for i in range(10000):
    # same request except call-id; rebuilding costs only generation side
    ws.append(req(extra=extra,body=b'',call='x'+str(i)))
d=base(ws)
b=json.dumps(d,separators=(',',':')).encode()
print('input',len(b),'wire',sum(len(x)//2 for x in ws))
t=time.monotonic();p=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'-I','-B','/app/submission/main.py'],input=b,capture_output=True,timeout=45);dt=time.monotonic()-t
print('status',p.returncode,'wall',dt,'out',len(p.stdout),'err',p.stderr[:100])
if p.returncode==0:
 o=json.loads(p.stdout);print(o['accepted'],o['live'],len(o['results']))
